newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins up on U.S. bonds rise, debt news.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins up on U.S. bonds rise, debt news.

text.p: Russian MinFin bonds edged up on Thursday after a rise in U.S. 30-year Treasuries and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's comments on debt, dealers said.
U.S. Treasuries opened higher as foreign players returned to the market.
Chernomyrdin told Swiss businessmen on Wednesday an agreement on rescheduling Russia's 385 million Swiss franc debt to Switzerland would be signed on Thursday.
He also said work was continuing on the solution of questions related to unguaranteed commercial bank debts, reconfirming Russia's position that it will pay off all its debts.
"All tranches rose slightly on non-aggressive demand," said Andrei Golitsin, MinFin department head at Natsionalny Rezervny Bank.
Dealers forecast mixed trading until February 4-5, when the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee would meet to decide on whether it should raise its interest rates.
"Now the market is very nervous," Golitsin said. "No one knows what to do and Russian banks prefer not to hold big positions in MinFins."
Alexei Denisov, a dealer at Bank Imperial, forecast growth in MinFins, if the Federal Reserve decision is to the market's liking.
"Russia has the biggest potential, as it has the biggest spread compared to U.S. Treasuries," he said.
